items.title: Understanding Number Play
items.explanation: Number play involves determining the number of people in front of each person who are taller. For example, if a child is the tallest, they say '0'. If there is one taller person in front, they say '1'. This rule applies to every arrangement shown in the figure.

items.title: Determining Parity from Even/Odd Combinations
items.explanation: The parity of a sum depends on the count of odd and even numbers. Adding two even numbers results in an even number. Adding two odd numbers results in an even number. Adding any number of even numbers always results in an even number. However, adding an odd number to any collection of even numbers will result in an odd number.

items.title: Applying Parity Rules to Real-World Scenarios
items.explanation: In the example of Martin and Maria, their ages are consecutive numbers (e.g., 51 and 52). Since one is even and one is odd, their sum must be odd. However, 112 is an even number, so it is impossible for two consecutive integers to add up to 112.
